stories.title: Buffalo Sabres Top 25 Under 25: #15 Prokhor Poltapov
stories.summary:
The Top 25 Under 25 is a collaboration by members of the Die By The Blade community. 92 readers ranked Buffalo Sabres players under the age of 25 as of August 1, 2026. Each participant used their own metric of current ability and production to rank each player.



Prokhor Poltapov



Drafted: 2021, BUF (33rd overall), 2nd round, 1st pick



Position: Left wing/Right wing (shoots right)



Born: 2/1/2003 (Age: 23) St. Petersburg, RUS



2025-2026 stats: GP 68 G 16 A 24 PTS 40 +5, CSKA Moskva



2025 T25U25 Ranking: 21st last year



This one has been a long time coming, with one more year of patience required.



Prokhor Poltapov, drafted way back in 2021 (Kevyn Adams’ second draft as Sabres general manager) is finally starting to look like the player Buffalo hoped it was getting with the 33rd overall pick. I nearly wrote him off myself a few years ago, but Poltapov has steadily developed and has now put together back-to-back 40-point seasons with CSKA Moscow.



The bad news? We still have to wait on this polarizing player. Poltapov has one season remaining on his KHL contract, running through 2026-27.



The good news? He shouldn’t need much, if any, AHL seasoning when he finally shows up. Poltapov has been playing against men for years now, and that experience should have him well prepared for the transition to North American hockey.







Buffalo’s brass views him as a versatile, middle-six “plug-and-play” forward. A spot could be ready and waiting for him when Jason Zucker’s contract expires next year. He should be able to step right in and contribute, especially with the ability to play either wing. After such a long and mostly forgotten wait, it almost feels like the Sabres will be getting an unexpected freebie player when it happens.



Prokhor was drafted at 6-foot-0 and 176 pounds, and those are still the only listed measurements I can find today. I have to believe he’s filled out physically over the past five years, but there doesn’t appear to be an update available. At 23, however, he should be much more physically mature than the teenager Buffalo drafted back in 2021.









Poltapov is a high-energy forward who does a lot of things right. He is highly competitive, has explosive acceleration and brings a physical, net-driving presence to his game. He can score goals, set them up and isn’t afraid to throw the occasional hit. He is also effective on the penalty kill. There is a lot to like about this resourceful player.



At this point, his arrival feels less like a possibility and more like a foregone conclusion. The wait is almost over, and Buffalo should finally get to see what Poltapov can bring to the organization next year.

Buffalo Sabres Top 25 Under 25: #16 Riley Fiddler-Schultz
stories.summary:
The Top 25 Under 25 is a collaboration by members of the Die By The Blade community. 92 readers ranked Buffalo Sabres players under the age of 25 as of August 1, 2026. Each participant used their own metric of current ability and production to rank each player.



Riley Fiddler-Schultz



Drafted: Undrafted



Size: 6′, 201 lbs



Position: Center (shoots left)



Born: 5/13/2002 (Age: 24) Edmonton, AB



2025-2026 stats: GP 65 G 21 A 18 PTS 39, Rochester Americans



2025 T25U25 Ranking: N/A



Back-to-back Schultz’s, and the only double-barreled last name on this list, meet Riley Fiddler-Schultz.



‘The Fiddler’ is also very likely to be the only undrafted prospect on this list, and has certainly done his time working his way up the hockey food chain to stand on the cusp of the big league. 



After five seasons in the WHL, the last two where he scored at a PPG rate for the Calgary Hitmen, Fiddler-Schultz went undrafted in 2023 but was picked up by the Sabres organization. A season in the ECHL followed with the Jacksonville Icemen where he potted 23 goals and 20 assists in 51 games, and earned a callup to Rochester the next season getting 13 G and 13 A in 51 games again.  



The Sabres acknowledged his growth by giving him a two-year contract which saw him finish the 2025–26 AHL season tied for second on the Amerks with 21 goals in 62 games, along with 16 assists. The forward earned the team’s nomination as the sole finalist for the AHL’s Yanick Dupré Memorial Award (Man of the Year), and established himself as a much-loved member of the team getting named the IOA/Specialty Man of the Year award for his heavy fan engagement and community work.




Man of the people, Amerks Man of the Year – Riley Fiddler-Schultz 👏 #LetsGoAmerks📰  READ MORE | https://t.co/uu01vL05YS pic.twitter.com/ZDxUIrmk46— Rochester Americans (@AmerksHockey) April 14, 2026




For the upcoming 2026–27 NHL season, Fiddler-Schultz projects as a primary call-up option and organizational depth forward for the Sabres. With elite prospects like Konsta Helenius and Noah Östlund graduating to the NHL, the center will be heavily relied upon as a top offensive and leadership presence in Rochester.



He plays a hard-nosed, 200-foot game at center, and his strength around the net and puck-tipping capabilities should translate well to a bottom-six role in the NHL. The forward has been noted for his high hockey IQ and professional poise, attributes shared with his uncle, longtime NHL veteran Vern Fiddler.









Fiddler-Schultz is another hardworking, high-character hockey player that the Sabres’ prospect pool seems littered with, and given his undrafted background, you know he’s not taking a single day that he’s here for granted.

Good Night / Bad Night - Pre-season Game 2
stories.summary:
The Bills thrashed the Browns to move to 2-0 in pre-season. Brandon Beane said they wanted to decide any remaining starter battles this week, so let's get into how things looked. 



	 



	Good Night for...



	 



	Kyle Allen - It's fair to say I am not Kyle Allen's biggest fan, but over the past two weeks he has played well enough to a) remove any hint of competition for the backup spot and b) give his teammates and coaches some confidence, one would presume, that he can go into a game and perform if needed. He layered one really nice throw into Trent Sherfield between defenders in the second quarter that was the highlight of his day - but he has also done a really nice job both weeks with executing play action - especially where the Bills roll him out and give him half field reads. I'm not sure how sustainable that plan is if you have to use it multiple weeks... but give him his due this has been a good pre-season.



	 



	Tylan Grable - Grable wasn't perfect on the night but he demonstrated he is healthy enough to play and also that he is a better NFL tackle right now that rookie Jude Bowry. He is clearly the Bills OT3 going into the season and will be that important swing guy should anything happen to either starter. The key for him now is staying clear of injuries which have affected him the past two seasons. 



	 



	Trent Sherfield - Sherfield had four receptions for 54 yards and was clearly the de-facto #1 on the night for Kyle Allen. And I am starting to see a route to the roster, even if it is a narrow path. The Bills top five receivers are set (Moore, Coleman, Shakir, Palmer, Bell) but there is potentially a 6th spot available. If they do keep a 6th receiver it is because that guy contributes in some way on special teams. I still see Mercole Hardman having the inside track to be their punt returner, however, the Bills clearly would like Ray David to add punt returning to his all pro kick returning from 2025.... which would open that spot up. And we know Sherfield is a really solid special teamer on coverage teams. That is his only path - as the 6th receiver who plays teams and is a break glass in case of emergency pass catcher... but I am more open to the idea than I was 2 weeks ago. 



	 



	Kaleb Elams-Orr - Some people were predictably upset when I said he had a poor game last Saturday, but it's a fact. He did. No such problems tonight. I thought he looked way more like the player we have seen clips of from camp - fast, decisive and powerful. Interesting also that he started the game with Keonta Jenkins and then they were replaced by Dorian Williams partnering Joe Andreessen. I'm not sure if that was just the Bills wanting to look at different combinations and actually other than Jenkins (who was rough in coverage) they all did pretty well. Would they consider KEO and Bernard (both of whom they seem to want at MIKE) as a possible starting combo? Not sure, but I think the second starting inside 'backer is one of the most intriguing questions still to be answered.



	 



	Tommy Doman - When you draft a specialist (kicker or punter) you always presume that person is likely to end up the starter. We didn't get a chance to see either Doman or the veteran Mitch Wishnowsky punt last week vs the Panthers but both punted really nicely tonight. Doman had a good first half and then Wishnowsky with one attempt hit a 59 yarder in the second half. But ties in this race go to Doman and his holding for Tyler Bass (which he did not do in college) has been on point so far too. I feel a bit for Wishnowsky who is definitely good enough to start somewhere (he was 7th in the League for percentage of punts inside the 20 last year) but the rook looks good and the Bills haven't really had a consistent reliable multiple year punter since Brian Moorman moved on. 



	 



	 



	Bad Night for...



	 



	Defensive Line Position Battle - I'll start with the most important negative of the night which is that in at least a couple of the Bills big starting position battles we are still not seeing much separation. On the defensive line TJ Sanders had a couple of nice plays early, and Landon Jackson had a good tackle for loss in a goalline scenario but both look to me more like rotational pieces than starters right now. Sanders had some run defense reps he'd want back and Landon is getting almost zero change in pass rush scenarios. Can they get enough production by platooning the two next to Oliver and Walker? Maybe. But right now this is the weakest starting spot on the team. 



	 



	Left Guard Position Battle - And left guard is only just behind as a position battle of concern. I didn't think either Alec Anderson or Austin Corbett looked great. Indeed I think there is an argument to be made that the best guard on display for the Bills tonight was Nick Broeker (who played well last week too but remains marooned with the 3rd stringers) cosely followed by rookie Ar'maj Reed-Adams whose pass pro in particular was nice and solid. If you tell me I have to choose one of Anderson or Corbett to start week 1 right now I'm probably going Anderson just for familiarity with what we run but not with much confidence and I'd definitely be inclined to keep Reed-Adams on the 53 and maybe even let him work his way onto the field at some point if the older guys aren't producing. I still think it is impossible that Corbett (if he doesn't win the job) is cut by the way and they try and stash him on the PS as he won't be subject to waivers.



	 



	Geno Stone - I liked the Stone signing when they made it. The idea of an experience vet who has started plenty of games behind Bishop and Gardner-Johnson felt like a sensible insurance policy. Others did, at the time, point out he has started on the Bengals defense the last two years - which should be enough reason to stay away. They might have been right. I thought he was below average last week and worse tonight. Totally lost in coverage, and gave up yards after contact when whiffing on a tackle. He is moving into roster danger territory for me at this point. Although the fact that Hamlin hasn't been much better might save him.



	 



	Jude Bowry - Bowry had a rough debut last week at left tackle and was this week switched to the right side. That doesn't have to be a result of his struggles, it could have been a plan given they are essentially looking for their #1 swing tackle. But this was another poor display. Bowry was my OT9 in the draft but I did wonder whether foot speed might necessitate a move inside at the NFL level. Given they are not getting what they need at left guard I'd like to see Bowry play some inside reps in pre-season game three - because he has given up sacks where his feet have got stuck and guys have breezed past him both weeks at tackle. Right now he looks a major project. 



	 



	Jordan Hancock - I don't think it's been the pre-season Hancock would have hoped for to this point either. Any thought about him pushing Dee Alford for the #1 nickel job is long since dismissed, despite the Bills seemingly committing playing that spot rather than safety where he was used last season. He has looked a little lost in coverage through two games. The Browns touchdown was something of a communication breakdown between Hancock and Kani Walker (who came to earth with a bump this week too) but it one of them definitely misplayed their responsibility - looked to me like it was Jordan. He also missed a tackle on a swing pass which given the emphases Jim Leonhard has put on tackling is not going to win him many admirers in the building.



	 



	 



	One more to go... let's see if the Bills confirm any starting jobs this week!

The Top 25 Under 25 is a collaboration by members of the Die By The Blade community. 92 readers ranked Buffalo Sabres players under the age of 25 as of August 1, 2026. Each participant used their own metric of current ability and production to rank each player.



Ashton Schultz



Drafted: 2025 – 6rd Round (167st Overall)



Position: Center/Right Wing



Born: October 3rd, 2006 – 19 Years Old



2025-2026 Stats: GP 49 G 17 A 25 PTS 42 / Playoffs GP 6 G 4 A 2 PTS 10, USHL



2025 T25U25 Ranking: Unranked



Ashton Schultz makes his debut on our list after a solid year and a strong finish to his USHL career. He set career highs in goals and points while playing 9 less games than in the 2024-2025 season. He was traded mid-season to the Sioux City Musketeers where he produced over a point per game in 17 regular season games and was a point per game player in the playoffs. He also put up 6 points in 5 games at the World Junior A Classic which helped team USA to secure the gold medal in the tournament.




Ashton Schultz got in on all four Chicago goals with his first USHL hat trick plus an assist as the Steel doubled Fargo 4-2. Schultz is ramping up before joining Team USA for the World Junior A Challenge, which begins 12/7 in Trois-Rivières, Quebec. pic.twitter.com/Xtr8zP3gCF— Kris Baker (@SabresProspects) November 29, 2025




Schultz is known for his 200-foot game and doesn’t take the finer details of his game for granted. His coach in Sioux City called him a “rink rat” and was impressed with his hockey IQ and playmaking ability. Those skills should translate well as he moves up from the USHL to college. Schultz will play at the University of North Dakota this upcoming season. He’ll have the opportunity to grow his game and build upon his solid foundation while playing in the highly competitive NCHC.

Buffalo Sabres Top 25 Under 25: #18 Vsevolod Komarov
stories.summary:
The Top 25 Under 25 is a collaboration by members of the Die By The Blade community. 92 readers ranked Buffalo Sabres players under the age of 25 as of August 1, 2026. Each participant used their own metric of current ability and production to rank each player.



Vsevolod Komarov



Drafted: 2022, BUF (134th overall), 5th round pick



Size: 6’4″, 208 lbs



Position: Defenseman (shoots right)



Born: 1/11/2004 (Age: 22) Chelyabinsk, Russia



2025-2026 stats: GP 55 G 4 A 7 PTS 11, Rochester Americans



2025 T25U25 Ranking: 17th



And just like that we’re back to defensemen.



Vsevolod Komarov has had a couple of years of seasoning with the Amerks without being called up to suit up for the Buffalo Sabres, despite the senior club’s severe shortage of right-handed dmen. That should tell you how patient they are willing to be with the hulking Russian who has been biding his time to get his shot. Buffalo signed Komarov on an entry-level contract in June 2023 sensing his potential, which gives Buffalo this year to decide where exactly he fits on this defensively-loaded roster.









A Sabres fifth-round pick (134th overall) in the 2022 NHL Draft, the Chelyabinsk-born defenseman played his minor hockey with the Metallurg Magnitogorsk organization before making the switch to Quebec Remparts after being selected in the CHL Import Draft. His first season was focused on being more conscientious of the defensive side of the game, picking up 19 points (2 G, 17 A) in 60 QMJHL games, but the brakes came off the next season with 12 goals and 27 assists, including the game-winning goal for Quebec in the Memorial Cup final. 



His dominance in the QMJHL was such that when the new leadership team took over at the Drummondville Voltigeurs, they made trading for Komarov a priority, and the blockbuster trade worked out for them with the defenseman enjoying another stellar season. The Russian dman won his second consecutive QMJHL Championship, picking up the Emile Bouchard Trophy as the QMJHL’s top defenseman and more than compensated for the injury of star forward Maveric Lamoureux, also winning the QMJHL playoffs MVP with another 15 points in 19 games. While he wasn’t able to win back-to-back Memorial Cups, his feat of 14 G and 55 A, and a total of 86 points in 82 games across two teams and the entire season was no mean feat. 



Sylvain Favreau, Voltigeurs’ head coach, from The Athletic – 



“I think he’s an NHL player. At the NHL level he’s going to be classified as a two-way defenseman but somebody who can escape out of trouble, make a first pass, bring a little bit of offense, and probably one of the best sticks that I’ve seen in my eight years in the Q, and I’ve seen a lot of really good defensemen.”



Sabres’ development coach Nathan Paetsch, also to The Athletic – 



“He has elite composure and hockey sense,” Paetsch said. “A lot of young (defensemen), they get the puck and they panic. There’s just no panic to his game, so he can make those tight-area plays in small spaces. A lot of D can’t make those plays at that size. Let’s be honest, we got a steal in the fifth round.”









Komarov didn’t have the best season last year for the Amerks, but few players did. With the constant moving of forwards up the interstate to Buffalo, Rochester endured a difficult season and trades further decimated the roster. The Sabres will be grateful they have one more year to evaluate the dman, and even with the roster additions, he should be on the top pair for the Amerks and quarterbacking at least one of the two power play units.  



2026 Buffalo Sabres Top 25 Under 25



#25 Simon-Pier Brunet#24 Topias Leinonen#23 Gavin McCarthy#22 Luke Osburn#21 Maxim Strbak#20 David Bedkowksi#19 Brodie Ziemer#18 Vsevolod Komarov

stories.title: Davison Igbinosun: The draft day hate was way overblown
stories.summary:
A lot of folks on here were losing their minds when we drafted Davison Igbinosun, and honestly, the reaction was way overly critical.



	 



	I get where the frustration came from initially. If you watched him at Ohio State, the grabby play and the flags would drive fans batty. But look at the actual body of work—the guy put up great stats, and more importantly, his penalties dropped off dramatically in his final college season once he dialed in the technique.



	 



	Everything we’ve seen out of camp and preseason tells me this kid is a pure competitor. Is he going to get flagged sometimes as a rookie? Probably. Is he going to take some lumps adjusting to NFL receivers? Almost certainly. But what you are getting is pure nastiness, legitimate toughness, and a guy who flat out refuses to back down from anyone. He’s got the ideal physical traits and he’s ridiculously sticky in press-man.



	 



	I mentioned this in another thread, but his real value is going to show up on high-leverage downs. When we dial up a blitz on 3rd-and-medium and the DC needs corners who can get in a receiver's face, disrupt the timing, and hold up on an island for 2.2 seconds to let the rush get home, Igbinosun is built for that exact role.



	 



	Yeah, it's just preseason, but you can't teach that kind of edge. I really like what I'm seeing from him so far.

stories.title: The fall of Captain America and the return of Christian Pulisic
Interesting comment from Leonhard's presser today
stories.summary:
I would recommend watching his entire presser if you get a chance. Leonhard is extremely bright and I get more excited about the potential for this defense every time I hear him talk. I'll be shocked if he isn't a head coach within three years.



	 



	This particular comment jumped out and feels instructive about where the defense is going:



	 



	



	
		Quote
	

	
		
			Jim Leonhard with some notable comments on Terrel Bernard:
		

		
			 
		

		
			“He’s so damn smart and sometimes you want him to turn his brain off and just go play free and react to what he sees rather than overthink it. That’s the biggest thing, it was a little more structured in what he was asked to do in the previous scheme. It was very much ‘I see this, I do this’. And just getting him to play a little bit more free was probably the number one thing. If you want to play the way we want up front, ahead of him, he’s gonna have to react a little bit more. And that was the number one thing he’s had to learn.”
		
	



	 



	It's interesting how Leonhard kind of takes a shot at the previous scheme. That wasn't his intention but it has to be said to get his point across.



	 



	For all the talk about the change to a 3-4, for me the biggest change is the change in mindset on defense and I think this comment speaks to it. With McDermott it was see the play unfold first, then react according to your strict set of rules. It was a play backwards not forwards kind of mindset that resulted in us giving up a lot of soft yards and frustrating 3rd down conversions. And every year we'd get to the playoffs and smart QBs and offensive coaches would know our rules and mercilessly take advantage of them.



	 



	Obviously every defense has keys and rules that the players have to follow but there is a middle ground between reckless and rigid. I think Leonhard has found the right balance and the results will show up in certain players looking better than they have before, the LBs being maybe the biggest beneficiaries of the change.



	 



	Ever since Brady took over the mantra of the coaching staff has changed from "do your 1/11" to "play free." It's an important distinction. Building a perfectly oiled machine is a nice idea, but great NFL defenses are made by players making plays. And Leonhard understands that his guys will be able to make more plays when they're playing on their toes instead of on their heels.

stories.title: Buffalo Sabres Top 25 Under 25: #19 Brodie Ziemer
stories.summary:
The Top 25 Under 25 is a collaboration by members of the Die By The Blade community. 92 readers ranked Buffalo Sabres players under the age of 25 as of August 1, 2026. Each participant used their own metric of current ability and production to rank each player.



Brodie Ziemer



Drafted: 2024, BUF (71st overall), 3rd round pick



Size: 5’11”, 200 lbs



Position: Winger (shoots right)



Born: 2/22/2006 (Age: 20) Chaska, MN



2025-2026 stats: GP 36 G 23 A 13 PTS 36, University of Minnesota



2025 T25U25 Ranking: 19th



What’s this, a forward?! 



In Brodie Ziemer, the Buffalo Sabres have a winger prospect whose background is littered with achievement and studded with leadership. A product of the storied Shattuck St. Mary’s program between 2020-22, Ziemer won the 2021 14U AAA USA Hockey Youth National Championship, finishing his time there with finishing with 217 points in 109 games. 



From there he went to the USNTDP Juniors for two years, ranking fourth on Team USA in scoring during the 2023-24 campaign with 70 points (27 goals, 43 assists) in 61 appearances. Next came the University of Minnesota, where he picked up 23 points in 38 games as a freshman, before moving to point-per-game pace last season with the Gophers, scoring 23 goals with 13 assists in 36 games leading the team in scoring and winning All-Big Ten Conference Second Team honors. His 23 goals was seventh nationally.



In all, he’s won gold at the Under-17 WHC (3G, 3A, 6pts), silver at the Under-18 WJC (3g, 9A, 12pts), and then gold at the Under-20 WJC (3G, 4A, 7pts) where he was also captain of Team USA.









Ziemer didn’t add any height last year, but did bulk up to a round 200lbs which makes him a compact unit that is not easy to bump off the puck. Dubbed Mr. Consistent by a former coach, it’s looking like he will be staying in college for another season.



A bulldog of a player, the 20-year-old is a ferocious competitor who showed his scoring touch this last season. There’s some razzle-dazzle there as well, and he’s not afraid to show it off. Where he still needs some more seasoning is in his own defensive zone, especially with attacking forwards as they cross the blue line and closing down the space they are being afforded. 









What is interesting about Ziemer is that he’s doesn’t jump out on your screen as a superstar. What is unique about him is that he’s good at everything. You know that kid in your school that was just solid at everything he touched? That’s Brodie. 



“He’s not the fastest skater, he doesn’t have the best shot, he’s not elite in any one category. He just does so much right. He’s just very good at everything.” said Nick Fohr, Ziemer’s coach at the US National Team Development Program to the Times-Herald.



“He just does so much right all the time, including just every detail, every day, every meeting, he’s just locked in. He’s that typical guy that just leads by example and everybody looks to. He gets along with everybody. Everybody respects him.”









Some more intangibles once again in a prospect group that the Sabres have a very good chance of producing more gems from. There’s enough in Ziemer that Buffalo decided to let him play another year of Gopher hockey to develop, before they will likely bring him to Rochester to play hopefully in the postseason for the Amerks. 



A unique nugget of information about Ziemer – he’s the only Gopher to have ever worn the #74 sweater in the college’s history. If he makes it to the Sabres and keeps the #74, he’ll join Rasmus Asplund, Jay McKee and one very mysterious prospect from the Tokyo Katanas, Taro Tsujimoto. 



2026 Buffalo Sabres Top 25 Under 25



#25 Simon-Pier Brunet#24 Topias Leinonen#23 Gavin McCarthy#22 Luke Osburn#21 Maxim Strbak#20 David Bedkowksi#19 Brodie Ziemer

Maxim Strbak



Drafted: 2023, BUF (45th overall), 2nd round, 13th pick



Position: Defense (shoots right)



Born: 4/13/2005 (Age: 21) Kosice, SVK



2025-2026 stats: GP 37 G 3 A 15 PTS 18 +20, Michigan State University

And you may ask yourself“How do I work this?”And you may ask yourself“Where is that large automobile?”



And you may ask yourself, “Do the Buffalo Sabres have any freakin’ forwards on this damn list?” I assure you, they do. Just not yet.



We have a batch of wingers and centers coming up soon, I promise. We are simply following YOUR votes! In the meantime, the run on defensemen continues.



Also noteworthy, today’s Top 25 Under 25 is officially the “Not Another RH Defenseman!” edition, and is brought to you by the letter D.



Of course it would be.









Here we go again, but at least the NHL favorability factor is picking up a bit. Like recent write-up Gavin McCarthy, Maxim Strbak was also selected in 2023, is also 21 years old now and was drafted at the same relative size of 6’2″ and 196 pounds. (he is now listed at over 200) He is also coming off three solid years of college hockey like McCarthy and is now turning pro. Strbak attended Michigan State though, another productive collegiate program like Gavin’s Boston University.



Buffalo selected him 45th overall in the second round that year. After three seasons with the Spartans, Strbak finished his college career with 46 points in 102 games and a plus 33 rating. He also helped Michigan State make three consecutive NCAA Tournament appearances while winning three Big Ten championships.



In 37 games last season, Maxim finished with 3 goals and 18 points in total. (he was a +20)







Michigan State defenseman Maxim Strbak, right, celebrates a goal scored by Michigan State center Red Savage against Michigan during the third period at Yost Ice Arena in Ann Arbor on Friday, Feb. 9, 2024.



.** As a sidenote, how cool a hockey name is Red Savage? (from the picture above) He sounds like one pissed-off mother F’er. You immediately picture a guy with a black eye, missing a few teeth, and zero interest in hearing your apology. He might just bite your face off your skull. **



In April of 2026, the Sabres signed Strbak to his entry level deal. He snuck in two games with Rochester to close the season, picking up one assist. He looks to be a solid addition for the Amerks on the blueline and should see increasingly big minutes as he adjusts.



Known for his physical, shutdown defensive style and strong skating, the Sabres really like what they see in Maxim Strbak. He is well-adjusted, intelligent, and brings an air of professionalism with him. He should fit in well down in Rochester as he continues to work on his game. His stay-at-home style of play will be a welcome addition to the organization, giving the Amerks another reliable defensive presence.



Good things are expected from Strbak in his continued development. This kid looks to have an NHL future in him but will it materialize in Buffalo?

David Bedkowski took a positive step in his development this past season. He set OHL career highs in goals, assists, points, and penalty minutes while spending the first half the season as captain of the Owen Sound Attack and finishing with the Ottawa 67’s.



The improved offensive production is nice to see, but his bread and butter is his work in the trenches. At roughly 6’6” 220lbs, he’s an imposing force in Major Junior and routinely throws his weight around. Even top OHL prospects have to keep their head on a swivel when he’s out there:




David Bedkowski lowered the boom on highly touted draft prospect Adam Novotny last night and got into his sixth scrap of the season (and second since being dealt to Ottawa) as a result. pic.twitter.com/pBXUhdiZw4— Kris Baker (@SabresProspects) January 31, 2026




He plays on the edge between hard-nosed and dirty and is no stranger to crossing the line. He had multiple suspensions this past season. Including playoffs, Bedkowski had a whopping 132 penalty minutes in 75 games. While the Sabres could use a bruiser on their blueline, he will need to exercise better judgement to avoid the Department of Player Safety from having his number on speed dial.

Two Thursdays ago, Bedkowski received five and a game for this big blindside hit on VAN prospect Kieren Dervin as Ottawa completed the sweep of Kingston: pic.twitter.com/IT6eR6C28D— Kris Baker (@SabresProspects) April 12, 2026

Buffalo Sabres Top 25 Under 25: #22 Luke Osburn
stories.summary:
The Top 25 Under 25 is a collaboration by members of the Die By The Blade community. 92 readers ranked Buffalo Sabres players under the age of 25 as of August 1, 2026. Each participant used their own metric of current ability and production to rank each player.



Luke Osburn



Drafted: 2024, BUF (108th overall), 4th round pick



Size: 6’1″, 189 lbs 



Position: Defense (shoots left)



Born:  9/9/2006 (Age: 19) Plymouth, MI



2025-2026 stats: GP 32 G 6 A 15 PTS 21, University of Wisconsin



2025 T25U25 Ranking:  Unranked



The Sabres pipeline is filled with young defensemen, and in Luke Osburn they have another one that has offensive talent, work ethic and leadership in buckets. The Badgers showed last season that they were not afraid to put the rookie on ice in key game situations, and Osburn delivered and then some. Trailing 3-1 with 4:47 remaining in the third period of the NCAA regional final, the defenseman stepped up from the point and slammed a goal home from the left circle. Just over thirty seconds later he was on the ice for the game leveler, and then again in the first shift of overtime as they scored the game winner. Wisconsin would lose to the University of Denver in the NCAA championship game, but Osburn has already shown that even at just 19 he can be relied on in pressure situations.



Osburn scored 10 goals and 41 points in 55 games with the junior Youngstown Phantoms in 2024-25, going on to become the United States Hockey League Defenseman of the Year and on the All Star Team. He then picked up six goals and 21 points in 33 games as a freshman with the Badgers, getting names to the Big 10 All-Rookie Team.









Wisconsin coach Mike Hastings has been full of praise for the youngster: 



“Some people talk about 200 feet, but he’s as comfortable behind our net as he is behind theirs. Those guys are hard to find. It’s hard to put a ceiling on him because of all the intangibles being in place.” 



His coaches emphasize that he still has to work on his skating, though his lateral movement has improved a lot last season. As one of the leaders on the Badgers roster, this season will go a long way towards defining what kind of player he could eventually become for the Sabres. 



Wisconsin assistant coach Nick Oliver called him a rink rat: 



“He’s just wired differently. From the time he wakes up until the time he goes to bed, he’s trying to find any possible way to get better. He’s one of the first ones into the rink most days, he’s one of the last ones to leave most days, and I think as the years have progressed, you’ve just seen his all-around game continue to round out because of it.”

stories.title: NFL Sunday Ticket 2026
stories.summary: Just curious if anyone here is renewing their Sunday Ticket from last year. Last year because I was a new customer, I only paid around $200 for the package. This year since I would be a returning customer, it's going to cost me $480 which I really have no intention of paying. My question here is to the people that are renewing that don't have Youtube TV, have you reached out to YouTube and tried to haggle with them like with Directv to see if you could get it at a cheaper rate? And if so, is YouTube biting? I currently do not have YouTube TV so unlike when I had Directv and could just simply threaten to cancel to get a discount. I can't do that with Youtube TV. I bought the subscription separately and it looks like if I decided to get YouTube TV with it, I could actually renew Sunday Ticket for $240 but that's on top of paying $54 a month for the YouTube TV subscription. Has anyone been able to get a discount on a renewal with just the Sunday Ticket subscription? And if so, what did you do to make it happen?
